subject: SIG questionnaire — logistics, artifact pack, and sample answers
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@acme-healthtech.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: security-request@acme-healthtech.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG delivery and artifact list (deadline 2027-09-21)

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement team needs the completed SIG questionnaire and the following artifacts to close our security review by 2027-09-21:

- SOC 2 Type II report (most recent)
- Pen test executive summary (last 12 months)
- ISO 27001 statement of applicability or certification statement
- Security deck / architecture slides (customer-facing)

Can you confirm you can deliver these and whether you can provide a sample of SIG answers for the high/medium risk sections (access control, encryption, logging)? Ideally we get the artifacts in a single secure share (Drive or DocuSign) and an answer pack for our security team.

Also note a small compliance ask: we need clarification on encryption at rest for customer KV caches (one sentence).

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of InfoSec Programs | Acme HealthTech
elena.morales@acme-healthtech.com

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: elena.morales@acme-healthtech.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: SIG delivery and artifact list (deadline 2027-09-21)

Forwarding Acme's request — they want a consolidated SIG pack + sample answers and a short encryption-at-rest clarification.

Plan I propose:
- Rishi: own SOC 2 + pen test summary (deliverables: SOC2 pdf, pen test one-page summary)
- Marissa: compile SIG sample answers and security deck, double-check any customer-facing redactions
- I'll prepare the secure Drive folder and DocuSign envelope if they prefer signed attestations.

Quick sample answers (to speed the review):
- Access control (Q: How are user privileges provisioned?): "User accounts are provisioned via SSO (SAML 2.0) with role-based access controls; least privilege enforced; periodic access reviews quarterly."
- Logging (Q: Are production logs retained and monitored?): "Application and infrastructure logs are retained for 90 days in immutable storage with alerting to our on-call rotation; critical audit logs retained for 1 year."

Attachments included in this outgoing email: SOC2-Type2-Redwood-2026.pdf (redacted), PenTest-Summary-Redwood-2027.pdf (exec summary), ISO27001-Statement-Redwood.txt, Redwood-Security-Deck-v2.pdf

Action items: Rishi to confirm redaction OK and any caveats on pen test; Marissa to prepare the SIG answer pack and a single-page encryption note for KV caches. Elena — if Drive is fine we'll upload and share; otherwise DocuSign for signed attestations works too.

- Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, elena.morales@acme-healthtech.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: SIG delivery and artifact list (deadline 2027-09-21)

Thanks — quick update from my side:

- SOC2-Type2-Redwood-2026.pdf: final redacted copy attached (contains SOC auditor cover letter and control mappings).
- PenTest-Summary-Redwood-2027.pdf: attached executive summary only (sensitive vuln details kept internal).

Regarding the encryption-at-rest note: our platform encrypts customer data at rest using AES-256 with customer key support via KMS (customer-managed keys available in Private deployments). For KV cache specifically: cached tokens are encrypted at rest in the same KMS-protected storage and isolated per-tenant; no plaintext persistence to disk. Suggest the following one-liner for the SIG: "Customer KV caches and persisted state are encrypted at rest with AES-256; customers may configure KMS-managed keys for Private deployments."

Two quick asks:
1) Marissa — can you fold that one-liner into the SIG sample answers?
2) Vanessa — I'll mark the SOC2 as "redacted for distribution" in Drive and add the audit caveats in the folder readme.

-Rishi
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@acme-healthtech.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, security-request@acme-healthtech.com
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG delivery and artifact list (deadline 2027-09-21)

Vanessa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the sample answers, Rishi.

Drive share would be fine. Please:
- Upload the artifacts to a single read-only Drive folder and share with security-request@acme-healthtech.com (we will not request the full pen test).
- Include a short README in the folder with the redaction summary and the one-line KV cache encryption statement.
- Provide the SIG sample answers as a single PDF or sheet with question IDs (our team prefers a single file for intake).

If you can get that to us by end-of-day Monday 2027-09-20, we can keep the procurement timeline.

Also: small request — can you include the contact for incident response (name/email) in the README?

Appreciate it — Elena
